A three-storey, under-construction building collapsed in Old Delhi‘s Chawri Bazaar, with several people feared trapped under the debris. Rescue operations underway. Photo: Sushil Kumar Verma
At least two bodies have been identified and several others are feared trapped after a three-storey building under construction collapsed in Gali Sattara, Sheesh Mahal, near Chawri Bazaar Metro station in Old Delhi on Thursday (November 5, 2026) morning.
According to the Delhi Fire Services, a call regarding the building collapse was received at 9.50 a.m.. Four persons were already rescued by locals and shifted to hospital before fire personnel arrived, they said.
At least six fire units, including water tenders and rescue vehicles, were rushed to the spot.
“There was no sound when the building collapsed. We realised something had happened only when we saw some locals running towards the spot,” said Shabaz, a resident of the colony.
“There was no sound at all. The building just sank. We did not hear the structure collapse or anyone screaming,” said Mirza Sahib, another local.
According to Shabaz, the building had been under construction for the past 2-3 months. The owners, who also live in the neighbourhood, were constructing it as their residence.
